items.title: Show HN: Classic Ads – A Chrome extension I made to make ads look like ads again
items.contentSnippet:
I made Classic Ads, a Chrome extension that makes Google search ads easier to spot by bringing back their old coloured backgrounds and labels.
The idea came after a family member was scammed from a deceptive Google Ad. I need to see ads for my work in SEO, but even I am getting caught out with how indistinguishable they are from organic results nowadays.

items.title: Show HN: Agent-Zero – Starter template for AI-native coding projects
items.contentSnippet:
Hi All,
Agent-Zero is a GitHub template that you can use for new coding projects that use AI-first development workflows. It includes the minimum necessary to nudge agents to write good code, work well in sandboxes, and get stuff done on GitHub (e.g. commits and PRs). It only includes a basic CLAUDE.md file and a few scripts and GitHub templates so it's very easy to customize. items.contentSnippet:
I created this online puzzle game where one daily real password from data breaches has to be guessed in Wordle-style. 
Once you solve it, you see how many accounts actually used that password (Source: Have I Been Pwned).
It's free, needs no sign-up, and takes a minute.
I work in digital forensics and I come across passwords every day, and the patterns are always the same ones.
Daily Crack started above all as a small awareness campaign on this topic.

items.contentSnippet:
I've made this app a while ago and now updated it with responsive UI and nice widgets.
Why did I make it?
During my travels to the US and Canada, I wanted to see prices in my currency. however, in both countries, prices are shown BEFORE tax. which adds more confusion.
This conversion apps uses location and locale to try and automatically provide estimations closer to what you'll pay based on your location.

items.contentSnippet:
What’s up HN?! I'm Benji, and I’ve been building Frink since ~April this year.
Frink is a desktop-first, open-source (MIT) app for running coding agents in parallel and multi-step workflows that start on their own. It runs on your machine (macOS and Linux) with your own provider login. It currently supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and OpenCode, but the latter 3 are in preview. No Frink account to use the app.
